_why: Operator 2026-10-25 (verbatim, voice-typed): "Arm the fixer and also a logger that tracks what was fixed, but this train should be no different than submitting in [to GitHub]. Somebody needs to monitor it, if there's little errors they need to correct it as long as they're adhering to our agents.md." Read by scripts/lib/self_heal_train_intake.py and scripts/self_heal_train_monitor.py only. Design + binding text: docs/ops/SELF_HEAL_TRAIN_FIXER.md (AGENTS.md section 28.14 draft). Changed only by reviewed PR.

arming._why: Live operation (deterministic remediations, fixer hand-off, coordinator tasks, sends) needs AGENTS.md at origin/main to carry Policy-Version >= min_policy_version with Status ACTIVE AND the section heading below with ACTIVE on the same line (AGENTS.md 21.0.0 section 28.14, PR #2128: "Arming is this section becoming ACTIVE; there is no separate guard grant."). Anything less = SHADOW: detect, log (fix_log rows with outcome shadow-proposed), propose; nothing is executed, launched or sent. The kill switch file stops all action. The model's output never arms anything.

sources.ci_required_workflows_source: the push/main runs of main HEAD (gh run list, GET only); any completed conclusion other than success/skipped/neutral is red

budgets._why: The monitor itself never calls a model. Model budget lives in config/self_heal_fixer.json (per job 4 iterations / 90 min / USD 12 reserved up front; 3 jobs and USD 24 per ET day; 1 job per cycle). The monitor adds per-day caps on what it may START.

deterministic._why: Known runner/infra flake (Docker Hub pull limits or pull failures in the Postgres shard, runner lost). One rerun of the failed jobs of that run, never a second: a repeat is a real failure and goes to the fixer.
log_patterns: The runner has received a shutdown signal

deterministic._why: A config/ci_gates/*.json file is not in canonical bytes (scripts/lib/ci_gates.render). Rewrites each gate file through validate+render; refused when any gate is malformed (that needs a human).
docs/INDEX.md is generated (config/release_train_policy.json generated[]): python3 scripts/report_docs_inventory.py --write-index.

docs/ops/packets/disk-standing-apply-20261024 pins the sha256 of config bytes (activation-input-sha256.json) and the review binds the pins file digest (review.required.json source_config_pins_sha256). When ONLY pinned config bytes changed, re-derive both (precedents 583512363, dcbdd0d08). Never touches the draft contract digest, the rules digest or any approval field.

regen_pr._why: A regenerate remediation runs in a throwaway worktree off origin/main under TMPDIR, commits only allowed_paths, pushes ONE branch and opens ONE PR labelled self-heal-fix. It never merges: the train carries it when eligible, otherwise it goes to the coordinator queue like any PR.
regen_pr.label: self-heal-fix

refused_scopes._why: A failure whose evidence names one of these paths is never fixed autonomously: it produces a P1 alert and a coordinator task. Mirrors AGENTS.md section 0 / 17 / 24.5-24.7 and the train's own rule set (train_self is blocked, broker held, guard/policy needs operator).

coordinator._why: The coordinator queue is the agent claim board task list (scripts/agent_claim.py task add --kind fix --source agent). Used for refused scopes, non-eligible fix PRs (the train's NOT_RIDING reason is held / blocked / needs_operator / BLOCKED_SELF_MODIFICATION) and escalations.

notify._why: Escalations (refused scope, attempts exhausted, ROLLBACK_FAILED, ambiguous reconcile, a train outcome that is not the fixer's to fix) are P1 immediately through the existing chokepoint telegram_alert.send_telegram(priority P1, producer self_heal_train_monitor). The raw failure itself (main CI red, train outcome, tester FAILED) is paged by scripts/delivery_failure_alerts.py once PR #2106 is on the release; this lane pages only what it decided (escalated / gave-up) and never duplicates that trigger. A fix that reaches fixed-released gets one short P2 note. The 10/15/17 ET digest reads the fix log (one daily line).

_train_stale_why: 2026-10-31 review round 2: the train_stale_reconcile rule called 'release_window.py train-reconcile', which does not exist (subcommands: plan, run, status, clear-stop). Removed: a stale train now goes to the coordinator (release machinery is the coordinator's), never to an invented command.
